read.sections.0.text.note: Last sentence: 'weather is what you get today, but climate is what you expect' rendered as 'điều bạn gặp hôm nay ... điều bạn có thể đoán trước'. Check the contrast sounds natural and kid-friendly.
read.sections.0.text.source: Weather is what the air is like at one time and place. It can be hot, cold, wet, dry or windy, and it can change in minutes. Climate is the usual pattern of weather in a place over a long time. To describe a climate, scientists usually study at least 30 years of weather records. Look at Sunrise School. Heavy rain this afternoon is weather. The fact that the rainy season has been much wetter than the dry season for 30 years is climate. Here is a simple way to remember the difference: weather is what you get today, but climate is what you expect.
read.sections.0.text.back: Weather is the state of the air at a place at a certain moment. It can be hot, cold, wet, dry or windy, and it can change in just a few minutes. Climate is the pattern of weather usually seen in a place over a long time. To describe a climate, scientists usually study weather records of at least 30 years. Look at Sunrise School. The heavy rain this afternoon is weather. The rainy season having much more rain than the dry season for 30 years is climate. There is a simple way to remember the difference: weather is what you meet today, and climate is what you can predict.

read.sections.0.simpler.note: Check sentence length and that 'mẫu hình' is understandable to a young reader.
read.sections.0.simpler.source: Weather is what the air is like now. It can be hot or cold. It can be wet, dry or windy. Weather can change fast. Climate is the usual weather in a place. It is a pattern over many years. Scientists look at 30 years or more. At Sunrise School, heavy rain today is weather. A wet rainy season every year is climate. Weather is what you get today. Climate is what you expect.
read.sections.0.simpler.back: Weather is the state of the air right now. It can be hot or cold. It can be wet, dry or windy. Weather can change very fast. Climate is the weather usually seen in a place. It is a pattern over many years. Scientists look at 30 years or more. At Sunrise School, heavy rain today is weather. The wet rainy season every year is climate. Weather is what you meet today. Climate is what you can predict.

read.sections.1.text.note: 'đường xích đạo', 'gió mùa', 'Nam Á', 'Đông Nam Á': check terms. Months written 'tháng 6 đến tháng 9'.
read.sections.1.text.source: A season is a part of the year with its own kind of weather. Far from the equator, many places have four seasons: spring, summer, autumn and winter. These seasons happen because Earth is tilted as it travels around the Sun. Near the equator, it is warm all year, so the seasons are usually rainy or dry instead. In South Asia and Southeast Asia, a seasonal wind called the monsoon brings heavy rain for several months. In India, for example, most of the year's rain falls between June and September.
read.sections.1.text.back: A season is a part of the year with its own kind of weather. Far from the equator, many places have four seasons: spring, summer, autumn and winter. These seasons exist because the Earth is tilted as it goes around the Sun. Near the equator, it is warm all year, so the seasons are often a rainy season or a dry season. In South Asia and Southeast Asia, a seasonal kind of wind called the monsoon brings heavy rain for a few months. For example in India, most of the year's rainfall falls from June to September.

read.sections.1.simpler.note: Equator explained as 'đường vòng quanh giữa Trái Đất'; check this is clear.
read.sections.1.simpler.source: A season is a part of the year. Each season has its own weather. Some places have four seasons. They are spring, summer, autumn and winter. Earth tips a little to one side as it goes around the Sun. This makes the seasons. The equator is a line around Earth's middle. Places near it are warm all year. There, seasons are wet or dry. In India, a wind called the monsoon brings rain. Most rain falls from June to September.
read.sections.1.simpler.back: A season is a part of the year. Each season has its own weather. Some places have four seasons. They are spring, summer, autumn and winter. The Earth is tilted a little to one side as it goes around the Sun. This makes the seasons. The equator is a circle line around the middle of the Earth. Places near it are warm all year. There, the seasons are a rainy season or a dry season. In India, a kind of wind called the monsoon brings rain. Rain falls most from June to September.

read.sections.2.heading.source: People adapt to climate and seasons
read.sections.2.heading.back: People adapt to climate and the seasons

read.sections.2.text.note: 'herders' = 'người chăn nuôi'; 'summer and winter camps' = 'nơi ở mùa hè và nơi ở mùa đông'. Mali, Yemen, Mông Cổ: check place names. 'sự thích nghi' follows KEY_TERMS.
read.sections.2.text.source: People change how they live to suit their climate. These changes are called adaptations. In hot, dry places, such as parts of Mali and Yemen, many buildings have thick mud-brick walls that help keep rooms cool. In Mongolia, some herders move their animals between summer and winter camps. In many farming communities, people plant crops when the rainy season begins. Sunrise School adapts too. Covered walkways keep students dry, and water stations help on hot days. A good adaptation is based on evidence and works for everyone, including people who use wheelchairs.
read.sections.2.text.back: People change the way they live to suit their climate. These changes are called adaptation. In hot, dry places, like some parts of Mali and Yemen, many houses have thick mud-brick walls that help keep rooms cool. In Mongolia, some herders move their animals between a summer home and a winter home. In many farming communities, people sow and plant when the rainy season begins. Sunrise School adapts too. Covered walkways keep students dry, and water stations help on hot days. A good adaptation is based on evidence and can be used by everyone, including people who use wheelchairs.

read.sections.2.simpler.source: People change how they live to fit the climate. This is called adaptation. In some hot, dry places, homes have thick mud walls. The walls keep rooms cool. In Mongolia, some families move with their animals each season. Many farmers plant seeds when the rains start. Sunrise School adapts too. Covered paths keep students dry. Water stations help on hot days. A good adaptation helps everyone.
read.sections.2.simpler.back: People change how they live to suit the climate. This is called adaptation. In some hot, dry places, houses have thick mud walls. The walls keep rooms cool. In Mongolia, some families go along with their animals by season. Many farmers sow seeds when the rain begins. Sunrise School adapts too. Covered walkways keep students dry. Water stations help on hot days. A good adaptation helps everyone.

write.example.source: The records show that the rainy season has been much wetter than the dry season for 30 years. This is a fact about climate because it is a long pattern. I recommend more covered walkways between the classrooms and the gate. This would help students because they could stay dry when it rains. It should also work for students who use wheelchairs. So the walkways need ramps, not only steps.
write.example.back: The records show the rainy season has much more rain than the dry season over 30 years. This is a fact about climate because it is a long pattern. I suggest building more covered walkways between classrooms and the school gate. This will help students because they can stay dry when it rains. This way also needs to be usable for students who use wheelchairs. So the walkways need a gentle slope, not only steps.

watch.summary.note: 'khí cacbonic' for carbon dioxide (school term; some say 'carbon dioxide' or 'CO2'). 'khí đốt' for gas; 'nhà kính' greenhouse; Greenland and Nam Cực kept neutral. Check the flow when read aloud.
watch.summary.source: This video explains how Earth's climate is changing. Some gases in the air, like carbon dioxide, trap heat from the Sun. They work a bit like the glass walls of a greenhouse, which keep plants warm. People burn coal, oil and gas for energy. This adds more of these gases to the air, so Earth is getting warmer. The video says a warmer Earth changes weather patterns. Large areas of ice in Greenland and Antarctica are melting, and the sea is rising. Some places now get stronger storms and heavier rain. Other places get longer dry times. This can make it harder to grow food. The video ends with a hopeful idea. People can use power from the sun and wind, which does not add these gases.
watch.summary.back: This video explains how the Earth's climate is changing. Some gases in the air, like carbon dioxide, hold in heat from the Sun. They work somewhat like the glass walls of a greenhouse, which help keep plants warm. People burn coal, oil and gas for energy. This adds a lot of those gases to the air, so the Earth is getting hotter. The video says a hotter Earth changes weather patterns. The big areas of ice in Greenland and Antarctica are melting, and sea level is rising. Some places now have stronger storms and heavier rain. Other places have longer droughts. This can make growing food harder. The video ends with a hopeful idea. People can use energy from the sun and wind, a kind of energy that does not add these gases.
